chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed the Dhuhr and Asr prayers with the people when the sun had passed its zenith (midday), in congregation, without any excuse.

key_terms.حِينَ زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: When the sun passed its zenith (midday)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on combining Dhuhr and Asr prayers without an excuse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practice of *jam' qabli* (combining Dhuhr and Asr early) performed by the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) at the zenith of the sun without a specific excuse like travel or rain. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence for the permissibility of combining prayers at any time within the overlapping window of their respective hours, emphasizing the flexibility of the prayer times as established by the Sunnah. The mention of 'in congregation' further underscores the communal aspect of this voluntary combination, distinguishing it from the more commonly cited combined prayers during Hajj or travel.
